newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes end lower, grades gain against imports.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes end lower, grades gain against imports.

text.p: U.S. crudes ended weaker, consolidating in a market dominated by technical factors and traders waiting for new developments from ever-volatile Iraq, where Kurdish fighting continued unabated Monday.
Traders said domestic cash crude, and Brent in the U.S. markets were subdued and cautious, with light volumes.
Outright October West Texas Intermediate/Cushing deals were valued late Monday a few cents firmer than the NYMEX October settlement at $23.73 a barrel, weaker than Friday.
Domestic grades turned in a stronger session, gaining favor against foreign barrels thought to be uneconomical.
Weather played a role in trading, as Hurricane Hortense drifted to Puerto Rico on its way through the Caribbean.
Experts were waiting to gauge the strength of the storm, which closely follows the weekend slap at the U.S. Middle Atlantic seaboard by Hurricane Fran.
Besides Iraq and the developing storm situations, the domestic grade markets were well-supported by refinery interest against foreign parcels, traders said.
Traders said both sweet and sour sectors of the domestic market were done at firm levels. Business also accelerated gradually from a lackluster morning session.
Midland/WTI was sold at 8 cts and 9 cts over WTI/Cushing, and was talked late at a 7-9 cts premium.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sputtered early, but saw midday and afternoon trades at 36 cts and 37 cts over WTI.
Sour grades sold at minus $1.05 for Eugene Island, and at $1.19 under the WTI/Cushing.
Traders said October Postings-Plus were active, selling between $2.31-$2.35.
On the foreign front, sellers were heard offering Cusiana at November WTI minus 12 cts fob for mid-September loading.
Oseberg was also offered at November WTI minus 10 cts cif for October 1-5 dates.
On the Brent front, majors were seen offering Brent late Friday at 10-15 cts under November WTI, but the talk was sparse today, with dated valued at the last deal of 10 cts under the benchmark.
Paper Brent was sold only twice in the U.S. aftermarket. Traders confirmed a Oct/Nov was done at 65 cts, and a 100 lot parcel was sold on an outright basis for October at $22.56.
